1. The contract shall be awarded for a term of ONE (1) year from the date of commencement. 2. The first three (3) months of the contract term shall be treated as a trial period. Upon the satisfactory performance o f the contractor during this trial period, SCTIMST may, at its sole discretion, confirm the contract for the remaining nine (9) months of the one-year term. During this initial three-month trial period, as well as the subsequent confirmed period: If the contractor’s service is found unsatisfactory regarding food safety, quality, hygiene, or services, the contractor must re ctify the deficiency immediately before the commencement of the next operational shift. For deficiencies regarding statutory non-compliance or other administrative matters that inherently require more time to re solve, SCTIMST shall issue a written notice granting the Contractor seven (7) days to rectify the deficiency. Failure to rectify any deficiency outlined above within the specified periods shall constitute a material breach. However, staff required for night and early morning shifts, limited to a maximum of six personnel, may be permit ted to temporarily rest within the designated area located below the main canteen, subject to a formal written request for t his arrangement and approval by the canteen committee. No residential accommodation will be provided by SCTIMST to th e Contractor’s staff within the canteen/institute premises. Under no circumstances shall staff be permitted to rest or sleep i nside active food preparation, storage, or dining areas. 5. Pre- and Post-Service Arrangements Before the dining hall is opened for service, the Contractor must ensure that

o Dining hall, including all tables and counters, is clean. o Tables and chairs in the dining hall are arranged as approved. o The dining hall windows are open and all necessary lights and fans are switched on. o Food and beverages are ready for serving and properly displayed to minimise queuing. o After the dining hall is closed following each service period, the Contractor must ensure that the dining hall, counter s, wash basin area, waste bins and kitchen are thoroughly cleaned and fully prepared for the next service. o Staff designated for cleaning duties shall not be engaged for the serving or handling of food at any time. o All lights and fans that are no longer in use are switched off in order to prevent energy wastage. 11. The bidder should have a valid license / registration in India for running a Canteen/Restaurant as per applicable norms. 12. The Contractor shall ensure that no person under 18 years is deployed for any service inside the canteen or its premises. 13. The Contractor must strictly adhere to the medical and health compliance requirements prescribed by the FSSAI. o All canteen employees (manager/supervisor, cooks, servers, cleaners, etc.) must undergo a medical examination b y a Registered Medical Practitioner (RMP) before commencing work in the canteen. The corresponding Medical Fitness Certificates must be submitted as detailed in Clause 14. o As per the FSSAI regulations, annual medical examination and inoculation against the enteric group of diseases (as per the recommended vaccine schedule) are mandatory for all food handlers to ensure they are free from infectious a nd communicable diseases. The Contractor must maintain an updated record of these examinations and vaccinations for all its employees. o Any employee known or suspected to be suffering from, or to be a carrier of, a disease or illness likely to be transmi tted through food, or those with open wounds or burns, must be immediately excluded from handling food or any mat erials that may come into contact with food. 14. The contractor must submit the following information and documentation to the Canteen Committee within two weeks of the contract commencement. a) A complete list of all employees engaged in the canteen, clearly indicating their role, age and address. b) The Police Verification Certificate for each employee. c) A copy of the Aadhaar card of each employee. d) Proof for statutory employee benefit details as applicable. e) Medical Fitness Certificate of all employees issued in the prescribed FSSAI format (downloadable from fssai.gov.i n) and bearing the RMP's seal and signature. 15. The Contractor must ensure that any employee presenting with symptoms such as jaundice, diarrhoea, vomiting, fever

, or sore throat with fever; boils, cuts, sores, or any other open wounds or burns; discharges from the ear, eye, or nose or a ny other condition that falls within the scope of Clause 13, is immediately excluded from handling food or any materials that may come into contact with food. 16. The Chairperson/Convener of the Canteen Committee shall be informed immediately of any worker suffering from an il lness or injury. In accordance with FSSAI regulations, any such employee shall only be permitted to resume duties upon the submission of a fresh medical fitness certificate issued by a Registered Medical Practitioner verifying full recovery. 17. The Contractor shall ensure the continuous presence of a Canteen Manager or Supervisor in the main dining hall for ov erall supervision during every operational shift, every day. The person must be capable of managing day-to-day operations and resolving service-related and customer-related issues. 18. In the event of the designated Manager/Supervisor's absence, the supervisory responsibility must be delegated to a co mpetent alternative person, and the Canteen Committee Chairperson/Convener must be immediately informed of the identity of the alternative person. 19. The Contractor shall ensure that all sales of food and beverages to staff are mandatorily billed using an Electronic Billin g Machine/Point of Sale (POS) system provided by the Contractor. 20. The Contractor shall provide a non-cash payment option of the Unified Payments Interface (UPI) facility for digital trans actions at the canteen. Invoices/bills must be clear and complete in all respects, and issued to all customers for every trans action. Each bill must clearly and separately state the Goods and Services Tax (GST) amount as applicable. Compliance wit h all billing, tax, and payment regulations is mandatory. 21. The Contractor shall ensure that a competent billing clerk is posted to manage the necessary billing activities in all operational shifts. 22. The Contractor and the Supervisor shall report to the Chairperson/Convener of the Canteen Committee. 23. The Contractor shall attend the meetings convened by the Canteen Committee as and when required. 24. Any untoward incident in the canteen must be reported immediately to the Chairperson/Convener of the Canteen Com mittee with necessary supporting documents like photograph/video. 25. The Contractor shall maintain the highest standards of food safety and hygiene. Food items provided must be fresh and of good quality, hygienically prepared and served. 26. The Canteen is currently estimated to serve lunch to approximately 350 people on average on working weekdays. The volume of services required may increase when the new block of the hospital becomes operational during the contract peri od, and the Contractor shall have the capacity to handle this potential increase. However, the Institute provides no guarantee regarding the exact quantity of meals or items required during the contract period, as actual daily demand depends entirely on employee footfall and individual preferences. The quantities indicated in the price schedule (Annexure 1) are estimated volumes provided solely for the purpose of evalu ating bids and determining the lowest bidder. They shall not be construed as a guaranteed minimum off-take or a binding c

ommitment by the Institute. 27. The Contractor shall provide morning tea/coffee, breakfast, mid-day tea/coffee & snacks, lunch, evening tea/coffee & s nacks and dinner during the prescribed hours. The notified timings of the services provided in Annexure II must be strictly followed. 28. The Contractor shall provide early morning and late-night tea/coffee for staff on night duty in the hospital (details in A nnexure II), for which the Contractor is authorized to bill the Institute only at the approved rates for regular tea/coff ee. The Institute shall not entertain any claim or invoices for special tea or coffee charges for these services. 29. In addition, the Contractor shall provide mid-morning and evening tea and snacks in the Operation Theatres (OTs), ICU s, and Cath Labs in a common, designated place within each area, as instructed by the Committee. For these services, pay ments shall be made directly by the staff members at the time of purchase. The Contractor is not authorized to charge mor e than the approved rates for regular tea/coffee/snacks, unless special tea/ coffee/snacks options are explicitly requested by staff members. 30. Individual room service is mandatory for patients and bystanders staying in private rooms within the PMSSY Block. This service is strictly subject to direct billing to the individual customers (patients/bystanders) and must comply with the operational guidelines outlined in the section on Food Services Operation in PMSSY Block under Clause 77. The approved m enu list and pricing specified in the contract shall be strictly followed across all areas of extended service areas of the Instit ute. Outside of the mandatory private room services outlined, room service is restricted solely to authorized departmental req uirements. 31. Tea, lunch, and other refreshment services required during seminars, meetings, and other official events shall be provi ded by the Contractor based on advance requests from the concerned departments. Requests for tea, coffee, and other ite ms for seminars, meetings, or conferences with more than 50 participants must be routed through the Canteen Committee for approval. Bills for services provided for seminars, meetings, and other events must be submitted to the respective depa rtment or section and certified by the concerned authority within forty-eight (48) hours of the event’s conclusion. The Institute shall bear no responsibility, financial liabilities, or obligations to clear delayed invoices resulting from the Cont ractor’s failure to adhere to this submission timeline. It shall be the sole responsibility of the Contractor to follow up to ensu re the timely processing and release of payments. 32. For any private catering requests, personal events, or unauthorized bookings made by individuale mployees, the settle ment of bills shall be the sole responsibility of the individual client. 33. For both official departmental bookings and private events, SCTIMST shall bear no financial liability, responsibility, or o bligation for outstanding customer dues, unpaid bills, collection delays, payment disputes, or operational defaults arising d uring or after such events. 34. The Contractor shall provide refreshments for all official meetings, interviews, training programs, conferences and othe r official events in the institute, as needed. o Order confirmation: Telephonic orders shall be confirmed in writing.

o Timeliness: Orders shall be served at the specified time. o The Contractor shall provide up to two persons in neat uniforms to serve food items to the meeting attendees, if re quested by the department/committee ahead of time to allow for necessary arrangements. o All utensils shall be removed from the venue immediately following the conclusion of the food service. 35. The staff members on duty on Thiruonam day shall be provided with a traditional Onam Sadya for lunch in the staff canteen. The contractor shall arrange and serve the Sadya at a mutually negotiated and agreed-upon rate with the Cantee n Management Committee, subject to the approval of the competent authority. Similarly, for any other special occasions or institutional events where a special lunch is required for all staff, the Contractor shall arrange and serve the meals at a mutually negotiated and agreed-upon rate with the Canteen Management Committe e and approved by the competent authority. 36. The Contractor shall strictly adhere to the following food quality, storage and preparation standards throughout the contract period: o Maintenance of specified food quality and quantity of food shall be mandatory throughout the contract period. o Quality of the ingredients: Provisions, vegetables, fish, meat, and other ingredients must be fresh and of good quali ty available in the market. o Fish and Meat: Fish and meat shall be procured daily from the market and shall not be served in any form after 24 hours of procurement. o Rice: For meals, parboiled or raw, stone-less rice in sealed bags of reputed brands that comply with FSSAI standards must be used. o Storage: Vegetables, fruits, eggs, and dairy/milk products must be stored securely in the walk-in cold room availabl e in the kitchen. In strict compliance with FSSAI food safety regulations and to prevent cross-contamination, raw fish, meat, and poultry shall not be stored in the same cold room used for dairy and fresh produce. o The Contractor shall maintain dedicated, separate deep freezers exclusively for raw meat and fish. These units mus t continuously maintain FSSAI-prescribed temperature zone of -18°C or lower for frozen storage. The Contractor must maintain automated or physical daily temperature logs for these units, which shall be subject to periodic inspection by the Canteen Committee. o Strictly prohibited: The Contractor shall not use, store, or permit the presence of spoiled vegetables, fruits, eggs, or any old food in any form (raw, cooked or semi-cooked) inside the kitchen premises. o Food Preparation: Except as provided hereinafter, all cooked items served in the canteen shall be prepared i n the SCTIMST staff canteen itself. No cooked or semi-cooked items (e.g., including, but not limited to half-cooked chapathis) shall be brought from external sources or used for cooking or serving in the canteen without prior authorization. o The Canteen Committee may, at its sole discretion and in specific cases or exigencies, grant a temporary, written e

xception for the procurement and use of cooked or semi-cooked items from an external source. Such exceptions are s trictly contingent on the Contractor: a) providing certified proof of FSSAI certification of the external source; and b) agr eeing to supply the items at the rates pre-approved by the Committee. The Canteen Committee reserves the unconditional right to withdraw this permission for the use of externally sourced items at any time and without cause. Upon receiving notice of such withdrawal, the Contractor shall immediately and no later than the next operational shif t, cease using the externally sourced items in question. o Specific product specifications: · Permitted Cooking Oils: The Contractor shall use only fresh and filtered coconut oil or double-refined sunflo wer oil that is compliant with FSSAI standards and carries the ISI/ Agmark certification for cooking. · Prohibited Oils: The use of Palm olein, hydrogenated vegetable oils (such as Vanaspati), and the reuse of any oil are strictly prohibited. · Substitution: For using any oil other than those specified, prior written permission must be obtained from th e Canteen Committee. · Milk and Milk Products: Milk and milk products shall be procured exclusively from MILMA. For using any bran d other than MILMA, prior written permission must be obtained from the Canteen Committee. 37. The Contractor shall strictly adhere to the following: Taking cooked food from the canteen for use outside the I nstitute, including excess or leftover food, is strictly prohibited. Leftover food should be disposed of safely and as per stan dard guidelines. 38. Food waste disposal: Food waste, including food scraps and leftover food, shall be disposed of safely and immediately i n strict accordance with the Institute's established waste disposal guidelines. 39. The Contractor shall strictly ensure the segregation of all biodegradable and non-biodegradable waste, including plasti c, at source, storing it in designated, labeled bins in accordance with the instructions issued by the Institute. 40. Menu Management: The Contractor shall ensure that all food items are supplied on a rotational basis with daily varia tion and as per the approved menu (Annexure I). Any proposed changes to the menu, ingredients, or portion sizes must r eceive prior written approval from the Canteen Committee. The Contractor must also provide all vegetarian and non-veget arian items, including curd at the standard quality and specified quantity. (Annexure I) o The provision of mid-morning and evening canteen snacks shall include, as a minimum, one boiled item and one sa lad or fruit platter option. 41. The Canteen Committee reserves the right to modify the list of menu items as and when required. The Canteen Contr actor shall be expected to comply with the Canteen Committee recommendations regarding the supply of additional items, if needed. The Contractor must be prepared to serve any additional items suggested by the Committee. Similarly, the Cont ractor must seek prior written approval from the Canteen Committee to supply new items it proposes. In both instances, for any items not included in the menu in Annexure I, the final rate will be fixed and mutually agreed

upon in consultation with the Canteen Committee before being added to the menu. The Contractor shall ensure that the rat es of such new approved items are clearly displayed in the canteen. 42. Display of prices: The Contractor shall prominently display the approved rates of all food items in thec anteen. The realization of prices higher than the approved subsidised and displayed rates from staff, students or service personnel of the institute is strictly prohibited. The Contract shall be liable to termination upon short notice if it is established that exc essive pricing has been realized from any user from SCTIMST including its staff, students or service personnel. 43. The Staff Canteen is intended solely for the use of SCTIMST staff (including pensioners, temporary /outsourced staff, ap prentices and students). The general public and external individuals are not allowed to enter the canteen premises. Except ions are made for service personnel or contractors performing work within the Institute, who may be permitted access upo n receiving specific instructions from the concerned department. Similarly, guests occasionally accompanying employees a re also permitted to use the canteen facility. The approved rates for all services apply to these authorized categories. Acce ss for personnel or visitors from adjacent medical campuses is permitted only with the prior approval of the Canteen Com mittee. 44. The Contractor bears full financial responsibility for direct payment collection from users at the Institute-approved rate s, and SCTIMST shall not be liable for any unpaid customer bills or outstanding dues. 45. The Contractor must keep a Complaints and Suggestions Book in the canteen. This book must be accessible to users fo r writing submissions and available to the committee members for periodic inspection. 46. The Contractor must ensure strict compliance with the following prohibited conduct and habits by all employees as ma ndated by the FSSAI: o The contractor and all staff employed by the contractor are strictly prohibited from using or consuming tobacco, alc ohol, or any other intoxicating substances while on duty and within the premises of the institute. In addition, the sale o f any such items within the canteen premises is expressly forbidden. o The contractor and all employees of the contractor must refrain from smoking, spitting, chewing (gum or tobacco), eating, or drinking in all food preparation and food service areas, or in any room where raw materials and food product s are handled or stored. o Any breach noted or reported shall result in the person/s being removed from the shift immediately and reported to the canteen committee. Alternative arrangements shall be made proactively by the contractor to ensure that no servic e or shift is affected adversely due to the act. o In the event of such an occurrence, the institute reserves the right to impose a monetary penalty as per its norms and discretion, which shall be recovered from the contractor's payable amounts. 47. The Contractor must ensure strict compliance with the following mandatory personal hygiene and conduct standards prescribed by the FSSAI for all employees (food handlers) in the canteen: o Work Attire and Personal Cleanliness: The Contractor must ensure that employees maintain a high degree of person

al cleanliness, including wearing clean uniforms, keeping nails trimmed and clean, and covering any cuts or abrasions with a waterproof bandage. Any lost dressing must be reported to supervisors immediately. o All employees must be provided with adequate and clean protective clothing, headgear (caps/nets), face masks, glo ves, and suitable non-slip footwear. All items must be in good condition (e.g., free from tears or fraying material) and worn wherever necessary to prevent food contamination. o Footwear worn outside the food handling area shall not be allowed to enter the food handling area. o Where gloves are used for product contact, they shall be clean and in good condition. Protective clothing (e.g., glov es, aprons, hairnets) used for food handling and hygiene purposes shall not be worn or used for any tasks outside of d esignated food preparation and serving areas. o Mandatory Hand Hygiene Procedures: All personnel, including visitors, entering the food handling area shall follow t he prescribed hand hygiene procedures. Ensure that food handlers always wash their hands with soap and clean potab le water, then disinfect their hands, and dry them (using a hand dryer, clean cloth towel, or disposable paper). o This is required at the beginning of all food handling activities and immediately after: · Handling raw food or any contaminated material, tools, equipment, chemicals, unhygienic work surfaces or upon r eturning from any break or non-food handling task. · Using the toilet, coughing/sneezing, blowing their nose, handling money, or using thet elephone. · Must avoid unhygienic hand habits that could transfer bacteria to food products (e.g., scratching the nose, rubbing eyes, or running fingers through hair). When such actions are unavoidable, hands must be effectively washed befo re immediately resuming food handling duties. · Hand Hygiene procedures must be followed after any action where contamination of hands may have occurred du ring work. 48. The contractor must ensure that all servers adhere to strict hygiene protocols during service avoiding direct hand contact with food-contact surfaces, including the following: holding plates in the palm of the hand with all fingers underneath the rim, holding cups/tumblers by the handle or base and holding spoons solely by the handle. 49. The Contractor must ensure that staff do not wear or bring any loose or personal effects—including jewellery, watches, pins, bangles, or false nails—into food handling or preparation areas to eliminate the risk of food contamination. 50. The Contractor shall ensure that unauthorized access to food handling areas is strictly prohibited and discouraged. Aut horized visitors to the food preparation, processing, or handling areas must, where appropriate, wear specified protective c lothing and footwear and strictly adhere to all applicable personal hygiene provisions. 51. All articles stored or intended for sale must be fit for human consumption and kept properly covered to prevent any ris k of contamination. Utensils and containers used for food preparation or sale must not be kept in any area susceptible to contamination from impure air, dust, or harmful emanations that could render the food unfit for consumption. 52. All chemicals including insecticides, disinfectants, cleaning chemicals, etc.; must be clearly identified, labelled, and stor

ed separately and away from all food preparation, storing, and handling areas to prevent malicious or accidental contamination. 53. Operational Cleanliness and Maintenance of canteen premises: Dining halls, counter, kitchen, cleaning area, work area, and store/cold room must be kept clean and dry at all times. The Contractor shall ensure that the canteen premises are kept clean, sanitary, and fully maintained according to the requi rements below: o Regular cleaning of the kitchen, storeroom, cold room, and dining area shall be implemented by the Contractor acc ording to the following schedule: · Cold Room and Store: Once every week · Refrigerators and deep freezers: Once every week · Kitchen: Daily - after lunch and dinner · Dining Hall/Tables/Chairs: § Tables must be cleaned immediately after the table is vacated by users and at any time they are found dirty duri ng service. § The entire dining hall, including all tables and chairs, and the wash basin areas must be thoroughly cleaned and s anitized after every meal service. o Wash Basin Areas: Wash basins and the surrounding area must be kept clean, sanitized, and dry, continuously spot -cleaned, and maintained throughout the day. Large food particles and solid waste that could cause blockages in the w ash basins and drains must be removed regularly by the Contractor's staff to prevent plumbing issues. o Hand washing supplies: Liquid soap must always be kept available near the washbasins. o All containers and utensils must be thoroughly cleaned, washed, and dried at the close of services to prevent the growth of mold/fungi and infestation. o Refrigerators and deep freezers must be maintained with their respective internal operating temperature at the opti mal standard for food safety. 54. The Institute will provide cleaning solutions/soap solutions required for cleaning utensils, floor, washbasins, tables, and hand washing, free of charge, based on usage. All physical cleaning tools, implements, and equipment, including but not li mited to scrubbers, sponges, brooms, mops, wipers, and brushes shall be provided entirely by the Contractor at their own c ost to ensure the maintenance of prescribed cleanliness standards. 55. The Contractor shall make a daily checklist/log available for verification of the cleaning schedule compliance. 56. The Contractor is responsible for maintaining all drainage and waste collection systems in the kitchen: o The Contractor shall provide and maintain suitable bins for the disposal of food waste and general refuse by users. The bins must be kept clean, fly-proof, and positioned to maintain a neat environment and prevent littering.

o All wastewater pipe lines leading from the canteen must be kept clean and free-flowing at all times to ensure prope r sanitation and prevent backflow. o The Contractor must ensure that their staff carry out a daily routine of thorough collection and removal of all visible debris - food and solid waste (by pre-cleaning dishes and utensils) before they enter the drain in the washing area. Thi s pre-cleaning is mandatory at all sinks and wash points to prevent any large debris from entering the plumbing and drainage system. o In the washing area where gratings are present, the Contractor must ensure that the gratings are regularly inspected and cleared of debris to prevent blockages, particularly in areas prone to frequent clogging. If repeated drai n or pipe blockages occur due to the Contractor’s failure to comply with the waste management protocols, the Contrac tor shall be charged for all associated maintenance and repair costs, as per actual. The institute reserves the sole righ t to assess and impose the related maintenance and repair costs. 57. The Contractor shall be responsible for using and maintaining the biogas plant installed near the canteen, as per established standards. All biodegradable waste generated within the canteen must be utilized for the functioning of the pla nt. The Contractor must ensure proper segregation of waste and its subsequent processing through the waste grinder prior to loading into the plant. Any operational issues, damage, or malfunction of the biogas plant must be immediately reported to the Convenor/Chairperson of the Canteen Committee.
